content:
Hi all, we are happy to announce two very interesting closely related projects: M2F and ReasBook.

M2F is a highly automated, controllable, book-scale autoformalization pipeline and ReasBook is a textbook-oriented Lean knowledge base and engineering playground built on top of M2F.

Our goal is to formalize an entire book end-to-end into a compilable Lean project. Notation, concepts, and overall structure are largely inherited from the source text, so we do not rely on ongoing negotiation over global design during formalization. Human contributors do not need to hand-write Lean proofs; they mainly provide the natural-language source material and help with interface and style review at key points.

Our pipeline runs in stages:

statement skeleton → human polish → proof completion.

The focus of ReasBook is to make book content maintainable, extensible, and reusable in Lean, while staying as close as possible to Mathlib conventions.

So far, we have formalized the following books, totaling 272,132 lines of Lean code:

  1. Terence Tao, Analysis II (2022)
  2. R. Tyrrell Rockafellar, Convex Analysis (1970), first 20 sections
  3. Jiří Lebl, Introduction to Real Analysis, Volume I (2025 version)

We would love suggestions and collaboration, especially on:

  • Good targets: recommendations of textbooks well-suited to book-scale formalization, and advice on naming, notation, file structure, and other style conventions
  • Potential contributors: tell us which chapters or topics you’d like to work on, and we can integrate them into the pipeline and co-maintain

Links (issues and feedback welcome):

  • ReasBook: https://github.com/optpku/ReasBook
  • M2F source code (to be released): https://github.com/optsuite/M2F
  • Technical report: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17016

If you are interested in book-scale autoformalization, or have ideas for good targets and best practices, please reply here or DM me. You can also reach me at zichenwang25@stu.pku.edu.cn.
Perhaps a discussion thread at #Machine Learning for Theorem Proving > Discussion: M2F and ReasBook: a book-scale autoformalization (with a question :)
